Clicking the green dot at (19,18) caused the following:
1. A gray/dark circle appeared around the clicked green dot (the green dot at c1 is now surrounded by a dark gray ring — a selection cursor).
2. The green dot at c2 (18-21, 23-26) turned into a gray square (w→g)! In other words, the green dot to the right of the clicked dot turned into a gray square.
Wait, looking at the diff: (18,30),(18,31),(19,29),(19,32),(20,29),(20,32),(21,30),(21,31) changed from w→g. This is the green dot at columns 29-32? No wait, the green dot was at (18,21,35,38) — columns 35-38. The changed cells are at columns 29-32, rows 18-21 — that's the gray square at (18,21,29,32), which was 'w' (light gray) and became 'g' (gray)?? Hmm, wait, the original gray square was color 'w' (light gray). Now some of them became 'g' (gray)?
Hold on. Let me double-check. The original gray squares were color 'w' (light gray), 16 pixels. In the diff, cells (18,30),(18,31),(19,29),(19,32),(20,29),(20,32),(21,30),(21,31) went from w→g. That's a ring pattern around the center of the square at columns 29-32, rows 18-21 — the edge pixels of that square changed from w to g, meaning that square became a darker gray 'g'? No wait — if the whole square had become 'g', all 16 cells should have changed. Only 8 cells (the edge ring) changed. Hmm, actually the square's boundary is: rows 18-21, columns 29-32. The changed cells are (18,30),(18,31) top edge, (19,29),(19,32) left/right, (20,29),(20,32), (21,30),(21,31) bottom edge. So the square's edge darkened — maybe it's a "selected/active" highlight, or maybe the square's rendering changed.
And the big change: around the clicked green dot (19,18), a dark gray circle (G) appeared: cells (17,17-20),(18,16,17,20,21),(19,16,21),(20,16,21),(21,16,17,20,21),(22,17-20) became G. That's a ring of dark gray around the green dot — a selection ring. The green dot itself is still green (the center cells (18,18),(18,19),(19,18),(19,19),(20,18),(20,19),(21,18),(21,19) didn't change).
Wait, but in the image the clicked dot is shown as a dark gray circle with a green center — yes, a selection ring.
And the second green dot at (18-21, 23-26): in the image it's still green. Hmm, but in the diff (18,17) w→G and (18,20) w→G... those are part of the ring. The dot at columns 23-26 didn't change. OK.
So what changed besides the ring: the square at (18-21, 29-32) had its edge pixels darkened (w→g). Interesting. Maybe that square is now "adjacent to the selected dot" and got highlighted? The selected dot is at columns 17-20 (c1). The square at columns 29-32 is c3. Hmm, not adjacent.
Wait, maybe I misread. Let me re-verify: the original gray square at row 1 (rows 18-21) was at columns 11-14 (c0), 29-32 (c3), 41-44 (c5), 47-50 (c6). The one that changed is c3 at columns 29-32. Hmm, why?
Maybe the click "selected" the green dot, and the game highlights the next target? Or the square at c3 is a "key" that got activated?
Or maybe the game is: click a green dot to "activate" it, and then it moves? The ring suggests selection. The darkened square might be a coincidence... no, it's a coincidence.
Let me look at the image again: the first dot (left) has a dark ring around it. The second dot (c2) is green. The third dot (c4, columns 35-38) is green. The square at c3 (columns 29-32) looks slightly darker? In the image it looks similar to the others.
Hypothesis: clicking a green dot selects it (ring). Then arrow keys move the selected dot? The earlier RIGHT didn't do anything because nothing was selected.
Or: this is a "connect the dots" game — click dots in order, and lines are drawn?
Let me test: with the dot selected, press RIGHT and see if the dot moves.
